epics.name: AI assist (Pro)

stories.title: `ResumeDocument` contract — validator, canonicaliser, projections (Java)
stories.depsNote: R0.1. Size M. Owner API.
stories.story: As the API, I want one authoritative implementation of the document rules so that every write is safe.
ac: `service/resume/ResumeDocument.java` (Jackson tree helpers), `ResumeDocumentValidator` (schema=1; known section kinds; one section per kind except CUSTOM; id format; limits: ≤ 40 items/section, ≤ 12 bullets/item, ≤ 600 chars/bullet, ≤ 2 000 chars summary, ≤ 256 KB total; dates `YYYY` / `YYYY-MM`; returns `{path, message}` on the first failure), `ResumeDocumentCanonical` (stable key order, trimmed strings) + `contentHash`, `ResumeDocumentProjector.toStructured(doc)` → the `StructuredResume` JSON (DESIGN §4), `ResumeDocumentText.render(doc)`.

fixtures `api/src/test/resources/resume-doc/{full,sparse,invalid-*}.json` with expected `*.structured.json` and `*.txt` — these same files are copied to `packages/ui/src/resume/__fixtures__` in R0.4 (TS must match byte-for-byte on the structured JSON).
stories.tests: `ResumeDocumentValidatorTest` (every limit), `ResumeDocumentProjectorTest`, `ResumeDocumentTextTest`, `ResumeDocumentCanonicalTest` (hash stable across key order).

stories.title: Doc endpoints — create from profile/empty, GET with ETag, PUT with If-Match, template PATCH
stories.depsNote: R0.2. Size L. Owner API.
stories.story: As a web client, I want to load and save a resume document safely so that autosave can be built.
ac: `ResumeDocService` + `ResumeDocResource` under `/api/profile/resumes`: `POST /built` (creates `resume` kind=BUILT via `ProfileService.createResume` so the plan cap applies → 402 `RESUME_LIMIT`; doc from `profile_item` rows if any, else `basics` from bio only), `GET /{id}/doc` (ETag `"<docVersion>"`), `PUT /{id}/doc` (`If-Match` required → 428 if missing; mismatch → 409 `DOC_VERSION_CONFLICT {serverVersion, doc}`; validate → 422 `DOC_INVALID`; > 256 KB → 413 `DOC_TOO_LARGE`; writes `resume_doc`, `resume.parsed_json` (projection), `resume.label` = `doc.meta.title`, `resume.updated_at`, in one transaction), `PATCH /{id}/doc/template` (registry list of known ids as a Java constant; unknown → 422), `GET /{id}/doc/text`.
ownership — another user's id → 404 for every verb.
`ProfileVersion` moves after a content PUT and does **not** move after a theme-only PATCH (test asserts both).
stories.tech: `web/rest/ResumeDocResource.java`, `service/ResumeDocService.java`, `service/dto/ResumeDocDTO.java`; `ProfileService.createResume` gets an overload accepting `kind`. Autopilot cap constant `AUTOPILOT_RESUME_LIMIT = 50` added but gated the same as Pro until Phase 18 (comment).
stories.tests: `ResumeDocResourceIT` (Testcontainers): create/get/put/409/413/422/428/404, projection written, label synced, version-hash behaviour, Free cap at 3.

stories.title: PDF export — Chromium sidecar + `pdf.ts` + S3 upload via the existing file endpoint
stories.depsNote: R0.5. Size L. Owner web + ops.
stories.story: As a user, I want a PDF that is exactly the preview, attached to my resume, so that the extension can upload it.
ac: Compose: `chromium` service (`ghcr.io/browserless/chromium`, pinned) on the internal network only, in `docker-compose.prod.yml` + the shared-edge overlay untouched; `PDF_BROWSER_URL` env for web; `DEPLOY.md` section "PDF service" (health check, memory, restart).

`web/src/lib/pdf.ts`: `renderResumeHtml()` (static markup + inlined `resume.css` + base64 fonts) and `printPdf()` (connect over CDP, `setContent`, `page.pdf` with `preferCSSPageSize`, 20 s timeout, 1 concurrent + queue of 10 → 503 beyond); `POST /api/resumes/[id]/export {format:"pdf"}` streams the PDF to the client **and** uploads it to Spring `POST /api/resumes/{id}/file`, then `POST …/export-recorded {hash}` (new tiny API endpoint in R0.3's resource: sets `exported_at`, `exported_hash`).
export re-measures pages in Chromium and steps the ladder down ≤ 3 times when over target; mismatch logged.
Export button in the editor; the resume list shows "PDF out of date" when `exportedHash ≠ contentHash`.
stories.tech: dep `playwright-core` (web); local dev fallback to a locally installed Chromium when `PDF_BROWSER_URL` is unset.
stories.tests: `pdf.test.ts` (html render snapshot; `printPdf` mocked); manual: one-page fixture → 1 page.

stories.title: Onboarding wizard — `/profiles/setup` path picker, Upload + Paste steps, card-by-card review, finish
stories.depsNote: R1.1 (+ ui `Stepper`, `SwipeCard`). Size L. Owner web + ui.
stories.story: As a new user, I want to build my profile from my resume by confirming cards so that I never fill a long form.
ac: `ProfileSetup` with `Stepper`; `PathPicker` (3 cards); `UploadStep` reuses `parseResumeWithAi` / heuristic fallback and the consent copy from `ResumeUpload`; `PasteStep` (textarea → same pipeline, `text` only); `ReviewCards` — one card per experience/education/project with Keep / Edit / Skip, `SwipeCard` gestures on touch, buttons always; skills chip cloud with parsed suggestions; identity confirm card from `ParsedBio` (prefills, never overwrites a `user` provenance value without asking); preferences step shows the six `/welcome` questions if unanswered; `FinishStep` with the meter + `nextAction` + one confetti (reduced-motion safe).
nothing persists until Finish → one `POST /api/profile/items/import` (+ `PUT /api/profile`); abandon-safe (draft in `sessionStorage`).
entry points: dashboard "Build your profile" card when completeness < 40, `/profiles` empty states, the extension's existing "set up on the web" link target (`/profiles/setup`).
analytics events `profile_setup_*`.

Upload and Paste steps pass the extracted text through SensitivePatterns (T1.1) before parsing: SSN/ITIN, bank/routing, tax IDs, passport/visa/document numbers and birth dates are redacted from the text sent to the AI parser and can never become profile items; the review shows "we removed N sensitive values — we never collect those".
stories.tests: `ReviewCards` component test (keep/skip/edit, keyboard), import payload shape test.
stories.benchmark: Kickresume LinkedIn/PDF import, Simplify resume upload; card-by-card review is the shorter onboarding (landscape §4.1.4)

Parse check — "How an ATS sees it": deterministic PDF text extraction vs the document, lost fields listed with fix hints (Free) (G20)
stories.depsNote: R3.3, R0.6. Size M. Owner API + web.
stories.story: As a user I want to see what an ATS parser would extract from my exported PDF — name, contact, each role, dates, skills — next to what I wrote, so that a template or a layout choice never silently loses a field.
ac: Export dialog (R3.3) gains a "Parse check" tab: the exported PDF is run through a deterministic extractor (pdf text layer → section/field heuristics shared with the Free public check M5.3; no AI call, Free) and the result is shown side by side with the `ResumeDocument` projection; lost or garbled fields (missing dates, merged columns, skills not found, contact unparsed) are listed with a one-line fix hint (e.g. "move Languages out of the sidebar"); every launch template must pass with zero lost fields on the fixture docs (R2.3 gate); `parse_check` event with lost-field count.
The parse check never surfaces or stores never-collected values: the extractor runs SensitivePatterns redaction before the side-by-side view.
stories.tech: api service/resume/ParseCheckService (reuse the text-layer extractor behind the AI parser, without the model call); web ExportDialog ParseCheckTab; fixtures under api/src/test/resources/resume-fixtures/
stories.tests: ParseCheckServiceTest on the three launch templates × 5 fixture docs (zero lost fields); component test for the lost-fields list and hints.
stories.benchmark: G20 — ATS Verification ($5 one-time), Jobscan; Enhancv two-column templates fail ATS parsing (landscape §2.3)
